look_here_first: Find an OPEN flower and measure the entire slender perianth tube from its base to the expanded limb: about 7–17 cm long and only 1–2 mm wide. Compare A. obtusa, whose open perianth is much shorter (about 2.5–5.5 cm total). Confirm narrow wedge-based opposite leaves and the thin ridges of a mature anthocarp; closed self-pollinating flowers do not provide the same tube comparison.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Perennial dry-country herb or small subshrub with branched ascending to trailing stems; flowering habit and solitary versus paired flowers vary.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Mostly opposite unequal paired simple leaves, usually lanceolate to narrow triangular-lanceolate with cuneate or decurrent bases; margins may be wavy or crispate.

key_traits.label: Open flower
key_traits.text: Single petaloid perianth (NOT a true corolla plus calyx); very long narrow tube 7–17 cm × 1–2 mm, spreading limb roughly 10–20 mm across.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: One-seeded oblong anthocarp commonly 6–10 mm, with five thin often translucent longitudinal ridges and shallow paired grooves; inspect mature fruits under magnification.

key_traits.label: Reproduction
key_traits.text: Open chasmogamous flowers and reduced closed cleistogamous flowers may coexist; lack of a large open trumpet is not species exclusion.
